songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑octane late set with The Other One & Good Lovin' fireworks
ai_show_review.blurb: The late portion of the Halloween show erupts into high‑energy jams, highlighted by a searing 'The Other One', soaring 'Good Lovin'' transitions and Jerry’s pedal‑steel cameo with the New Riders. Phil provides a rock‑solid bass foundation while Mickey and Bill lock in tight dual‑drum grooves.
ai_show_review.review: On October 31, 1970 the Grateful Dead turned Pritchard Gym into a Halloween playground. After an understated early set, the late show ignites with chaotic crowd moments and a string of standout performances. Jerry Garcia tears through Workingman's material, adds a rare pedal‑steel cameo alongside the New Riders of the Purple Sage, and drives the band on extended jams – most notably the marathon 'The Other One' that morphs into a soaring 'Good Lovin'' transition into 'Next Time You See Me'. Phil Lesh locks in with his bass, giving Jerry’s adventurous chord voicings a sturdy backbone. The dual‑drumming assault from Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann fuels the intensity on both 'The Other One' and the second half of 'Good Lovin'', though the latter’s later section is sometimes described as overly drum‑heavy. While the soundboard recordings vary in fidelity – the Serafin source is raw but spirited, the Miller capture is crystal‑clear, and the Cousinit tape has low‑volume quirks – the musical moments cut through any technical blemishes, making this Halloween gig a memorable snapshot of the band’s 1970 evolution.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard capture that preserves the raw, high‑energy late show with standout jams despite minor track‑splitting issues.

key_highlights: Seamless 'Good Lovin'' → 'Next Time You See Me' transition
'The Other One' marathon jam with dual‑drum intensity
Jerry’s pedal‑steel cameo with the New Riders adds a unique flavor
Strong bass foundation from Phil and tight drumming by Mickey & Bill

band_performance.Jerry: Tears through Workingman's material with ferocious guitar work, adds a rare pedal‑steel cameo with the New Riders, and delivers complex, evolving licks even when volume dips.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a solid, supportive bass line that meshes tightly with Jerry’s adventurous playing throughout the late set.
band_performance.Mickey: Locks in tight grooves on 'The Other One' and 'Good Lovin'', driving the jams forward with focused dual‑drum power.
band_performance.Billy: Pairs with Mickey to create a thunderous, interlocking rhythm section that propels the late‑show energy.
